findings.title: DataLoader prefetch advances the allocation cursor past global_step, so resume misaligns the accountant's allocation epochs with the sampler's
findings.claim: RandomAllocationSampler._consumed is incremented inside __iter__ when the DataLoader pulls an index list, not when the trainer consumes the batch. With dataloader_num_workers > 0 PyTorch prefetches num_workers * prefetch_factor batches, so _consumed runs ahead of the trainer's global_step. The checkpoint stores that advanced cursor (`sampler_state = opaque_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler)`), and on resume the sampler continues from it while the accountant continues from global_step. From then on accountant step j is served by sampler slot j+p, so the accountant's modelled allocation epochs [m*b,(m+1)*b) straddle two of the sampler's actual epochs and a record can participate twice inside one modelled epoch. The reported epsilon is then below the epsilon of the mechanism that actually ran.
findings.failure_scenario: num_bins=8, sigma=1.0, dataloader_num_workers=2 (prefetch_factor=2 => p=4). Train 8 steps, checkpoint (global_step=8, sampler.consumed=12), resume, train 8 more. Accountant charges pld_at(16) = alloc(8) (x) alloc(8) => eps=3.127790 at delta=1e-5. What actually ran is sampler slots 0..7 (one full epoch) then slots 12..19 (last 4 slots of epoch 1 plus first 4 slots of epoch 2), i.e. alloc(8) (x) prefix(8,4) (x) prefix(8,4) => eps=3.392558 at delta=1e-5 (5.116893 vs 4.687320 at delta=1e-8). That is an 8.5% under-report; every further resume adds another misaligned boundary (offsets accumulate as p, 2p, 3p...). PoissonSampler is immune (per-step i.i.d. draws) and KOutOfTSampler is only made conservative by the same offset, so this is specific to the per-epoch allocation scheme wired in by PR #307.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:150-152 — `self._consumed = i + 1` then `yield bins[slot]`: the cursor advances when the index list is pulled, i.e. at prefetch time.
Measured with torch DataLoader (scratchpad/prefetch.py): `num_workers=0 after 1 batches: sampler.consumed=1` vs `num_workers=2 after 1 batches: sampler.consumed=5` — a fixed 4-slot lead.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4949-4953 — `sampler_state = opaque_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler) if ctx.current_sampler is not None else None`; no adjustment for the prefetch lead and no cross-check against `self.state.global_step`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1734-1735 — `ctx.current_sampler = from_state_dict(ctx.current_sampler, saved_sampler_state)` restores the advanced cursor verbatim; `_from_state_dict_random_allocation` sets `sampler._consumed = int(sd["consumed"])` (_random_allocation.py:211).

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3736-3746 — `kwargs = {"batch_sampler": sampler, ..., "num_workers": a.dataloader_num_workers, ...}`, so the prefetching iterator is exactly the one whose cursor is snapshotted.

Quantified with the native primitives (scratchpad/misalign.py): delta=1e-05: accounted=3.127790 real=3.392558; 3 epochs: accounted=3.742660 real=3.942553; delta=1e-08: accounted=4.687320 real=5.116893.

The accountant's epoch model is `full_epochs, remainder = divmod(n_steps, self.num_bins)` (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_random_allocation.py:142), i.e. it assumes slot == step mod num_bins with zero offset.
findings.fix_sketch: Either (a) make the checkpointed cursor the number of batches the trainer actually consumed rather than the number the DataLoader pulled — e.g. snapshot `min(sampler.consumed, global_step)` / carry a separate `delivered` counter incremented by the training loop, or (b) reject `dataloader_num_workers > 0` for participation samplers, or (c) on restore, rewind the sampler to the accountant's `global_step` (the allocation is O(1)-reconstructable from `fold_in(key, epoch)`, so rewinding is free). Add a regression test that checkpoints under `num_workers=2` and asserts `restored.consumed == state.global_step`.

findings.title: num_bins drift on resume is silently resolved in favour of the sampler snapshot while the accountant uses the new value, and the drift warning claims epsilon is still correct
findings.claim: `_from_state_dict_random_allocation` deliberately takes `num_bins` from the snapshot and ignores `template.num_bins` (a test pins this behaviour), while the accountant rebuilds `RandomAllocation(num_bins=ctx.expected_steps_per_epoch)` from the *current* args. Changing `train_batch_size` on resume therefore leaves the sampler on the old amplification factor and the accountant on the new one. `expected_steps_per_epoch` is tagged `drift="dp_relevant"`, but for `mechanism_kind == "gaussian"` — which is what `sampling_mode="random_allocation"` runs under — the policy only logs a warning, and that warning asserts "heterogeneous RDP composition still yields a correct epsilon", which is false for a per-epoch allocation whose sampler did not change. The dataset-length mismatch in the same function raises, so the guard is present but incomplete on the one parameter the module's own docstring calls "privacy-load-bearing".
findings.failure_scenario: Phase 1: dataset_size=1600, train_batch_size=200 => num_bins=8. Checkpoint at step 0, then resume with train_batch_size=100 => accountant num_bins=16, sampler still num_bins=8. Over the next 16 steps the accountant reports eps=1.789395 at delta=1e-5 (one 1-out-of-16 epoch) while the sampler runs two 1-out-of-8 epochs whose true cost is eps=3.127790 — a 75% under-report, surfaced only as a log.warning that says the number is still correct.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:205-210 — `sampler = RandomAllocationSampler(template.data_source, num_bins=int(sd["num_bins"]), n_steps=template.n_steps, key=RngKey(...))`; no comparison against `template.num_bins`.

packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:169-171 — docstring: "``num_bins`` is privacy-load-bearing — it *is* the amplification factor — so it round-trips through the snapshot rather than the template."
packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/sampling/test_random_allocation.py:152-161 — `test_num_bins_comes_from_snapshot_n_steps_from_template` pins template num_bins=4 restoring to `restored.num_bins == 8`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4273-4278 — the accountant is built as `dpsgd_acc.random_allocation(_u(nm), num_bins=_nb, n_steps=_ns)` with `_nb = num_bins = ctx.expected_steps_per_epoch` (line 3715), derived from the *current* args by `_steps_breakdown` (line 4468-4469).

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:5328-5344 — `if disposition == "dp_relevant": if saved_mechanism != "gaussian": raise ...; log.warning("Resume arg drift on %s (dp_relevant, DP-SGD): ... heterogeneous RDP composition still yields a correct ε.")`. `mechanism_kind = a.privacy_noise_mechanism` (line 1453) is "gaussian" for random_allocation.
Measured (scratchpad/drift.py): delta=1e-05: reported(num_bins=16)=1.789395 actual(num_bins=8)=3.127790; delta=1e-08: reported=3.050544 actual=4.687320.

Related open issues #320 ("Bind runtime sampling to amplification accounting") and #356 ("Emit and require a sampler-accounting contract") describe the general contract; this is a concrete instance where the library actively resolves the conflict in favour of the stale value and emits a message asserting the result is sound.
findings.fix_sketch: Raise in `_from_state_dict_random_allocation` when `template.num_bins != sd["num_bins"]`, mirroring the existing `num_samples` guard, and make `expected_steps_per_epoch` drift fatal (not merely `dp_relevant`+warn) whenever `sampling_mode` is a participation sampler. At minimum, drop the "still yields a correct epsilon" clause from the warning for non-Poisson samplers.

findings.title: RandomAllocationSampler derives its per-epoch stream with a bare integer fold, colliding with the split()-derived roots the trainer hands the noise and adaptive-clipping mechanisms
findings.claim: `rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)` derives the allocation with an integer-only fold and no string domain tag. `opaque.random.fold_in`'s own docstring states that a mechanism "folds one unique string tag into the key it was given, once" and that skipping the string root is "the failure this convention exists to prevent". Because `split(k)` is defined as `fold_in(k, i)`, the trainer's `quantile_noise_key, gradient_noise_key = split(gradient_noise_key)` produces exactly the sampler's epoch-0 and epoch-1 keys. Today nothing breaks, because the Gaussian noise and adaptive-clipping mechanisms apply a further string fold before drawing, so no terminal stream repeats; but the allocation stream sits in the shared integer-fold namespace, so any future mechanism handed the same base key and deriving `fold_in(key, step)` would draw the allocation's bits with nothing to signal it.
findings.failure_scenario: With `clipping_mode='adaptive'` and default `data_seed=None`, seed=42: the sampler's epoch-0 key seed is 6663219682538052210 and `split(key(42))[0].seed` (the AdaClip quantile-noise root) is the same 6663219682538052210; epoch-1 equals the gradient-noise root 2142789487919306769. Sampling randomness and noise randomness are then deterministic functions of one another's root key rather than being drawn from separated namespaces — the property amplification proofs assume of the sampling coins.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/sampling/_random_allocation.py:125 — `rng = np.random.default_rng(fold_in(self._key, epoch).seed)`.

packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:73-82 — "**Strings root a mechanism.** ... Skipping the string root is the failure this convention exists to prevent: ``fold_in(key, step)`` is the derivation *every* mechanism writes".
packages/opaque-engine/src/opaque/api/engine/random/_engine.py:115-118 — `split` is "Defined as ``fold_in(rng_key, i) for i in range(num)``".

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:1429-1431 — `quantile_noise_key = gradient_noise_key = key(a.seed)` then `quantile_noise_key, gradient_noise_key = split(gradient_noise_key)`; line 3688 — `sampler_key = key(a.data_seed if a.data_seed is not None else a.seed)`.

Measured (scratchpad/rng_check.py): `adaclip quantile key == sampler epoch0 key: True`; `adaclip gradient key == sampler epoch1 key: True`. Terminal streams do not currently collide (`noise/sampler seed overlap: set()`) because `_gaussian.py:16 GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD` and `_adaptive.py:29 ADAPTIVE_CLIPPING_STREAM_FOLD` are folded in first.
Contrast: `packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/dpsgd/noise/_gaussian.py:407` — `step_key = rng_fold_in(st._rng_key, GAUSSIAN_STREAM_FOLD, st._step_counter)`.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a module-level `RANDOM_ALLOCATION_STREAM_FOLD = "opaque.dpsgd.random_allocation"` and derive as `fold_in(self._key, RANDOM_ALLOCATION_STREAM_FOLD, epoch)`. This is stream-changing, so gate it on a version bump of the sampler snapshot (the state dict already carries `key_impl`). Do the same for `PoissonSampler` / `BallsInBinsSampler`, which use `np.random.default_rng(key.seed)` with no fold at all.

findings.title: The O(G^2) allocation transform is recomputed from scratch on every distinct step count, making per-log-boundary epsilon_at cost tens of seconds
findings.claim: `pld_at` is memoised by `horizon_pld_cache(maxsize=16)` keyed on `n_steps`, but the expensive part — `_native.random_allocation_gaussian_pld(noise_multiplier, self.num_bins, 1, native_cfg)` — depends only on `(noise_multiplier, num_bins, config)` and is identical for every `n_steps`. Since the trainer asks for a new `n_steps` at every log boundary, every call is a cache miss and pays the full geometric-grid transform again (plus a second full transform for the partial-epoch prefix). There is no `NativeCache` registered for this primitive, unlike the DP-FTRL b-min-sep path.
findings.failure_scenario: Measured cost of a single `random_allocation_gaussian_pld(1.1, b, 1, default_config)`: 33.1 s at b=64, 24.7 s at b=256, 19.6 s at b=1024. `_maybe_log_save_evaluate` calls `ctx.accounting.epsilon_at(ctx.target_delta)` at every `should_log` boundary, and `_predict_stop_step` adds ~log2(horizon) more probes at setup. A 3000-step run with `logging_steps=10` therefore spends on the order of hours inside the accountant, all of it recomputing the same epoch PLD.
evidence: packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_random_allocation.py:145-150 — the epoch PLD is constructed inside `pld_at`, so it is rebuilt per `n_steps`.
packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_pld_cache.py:242 — the cache key is `(config, self._pld_cache_key(n_steps=n_steps), n_steps)`; a new `n_steps` always misses.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:3958-3960 — `ctx.accounting = acc.cached(ctx.accounting); epsilon = ctx.accounting.epsilon_at(ctx.target_delta)` at each log boundary.

Measured (scratchpad/timing.py): `num_bins=64: one-epoch eps=0.629055 (33.1s)`, `num_bins=256: ... (24.7s)`, `num_bins=1024: ... (19.6s)`; and end-to-end `dpsgd_acc.random_allocation(...).epsilon_at(1e-8)` at num_bins=16 took 9.5-56 s per distinct n_steps (scratchpad/probe1.py).

packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/_native_cache.py — `NativeCache` exists but is only wired up by the DP-FTRL b-min-sep path (`grep -rn native_cache` finds no random-allocation user).
findings.fix_sketch: Memoise the epoch and prefix primitives on `(noise_multiplier, num_bins, released, resolved-config)` — either an `lru_cache`d module-level helper in `_random_allocation.py` or a registered `NativeCache` like the b-min-sep one. That collapses a whole training run to two transform evaluations.

findings.title: Module docstring claims the discretisation error does not accumulate across the exponentiation-by-squaring convolutions; the measured over-estimate grows with t
findings.claim: The header states "Crucially the discretisation error does **not** accumulate across them, which is what makes large `t` tractable." What does not accumulate is the *grid size* (`conv` renormalises the anchor and keeps `n` fixed — geom.rs:200-208). The error does accumulate: `conv` rounds every off-grid sum up to the next geometric grid point, so each of the ⌊log2 t⌋+popcount(t)−1 convolutions can inflate the value by a factor up to e^alpha, i.e. the loss by up to alpha per convolution. The crate's own `test_larger_max_conv_grid_tightens_bound` encodes that the bound depends on the grid resolution.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader sizing `max_conv_grid` for a large-t production run concludes the bound is grid-insensitive and leaves it at the default. Against an independent deterministic reference (value-preserving log-grid convolution, scratchpad/exact_ref.py) the full-epoch over-estimate at sigma=1.0, eps=0.5 grows monotonically with t: ratio 1.0043 at t=8, 1.0084 at t=16, 1.0238 at t=64 — roughly the predicted log2(t)*alpha behaviour, not a constant.
evidence: packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:13-15 — "Crucially the discretisation error does **not** accumulate across them".

packages/opaque-accounting/src/pld/pmf/geom.rs:205-209 — `let log_v_min = directed_log_add(a.log_v_min, b.log_v_min, dir);` with `directed_next(...)` applied per convolution, and geom.rs:270-278 rounds each placed sum with `pos.ceil()` under `Rounding::Up`.

packages/opaque-accounting/src/amplification/random_allocation.rs:780-801 — `test_larger_max_conv_grid_tightens_bound` asserts a finer grid gives a strictly tighter epsilon, i.e. the error is grid-dependent.
Measured against an independent reference (scratchpad/exact_ref.py + exact_full.py) at sigma=1.0, eps=0.5: t=8 ratio 1.0043, t=16 ratio 1.0084, t=64 ratio 1.0238.
findings.fix_sketch: Reword to "the grid size does not grow across them" and state the actual error budget (bounded by roughly (⌊log2 t⌋+popcount(t)−1) * alpha in absolute loss), so users can size `max_conv_grid` against a stated accuracy target.

clean_areas: Remove/add PLD formulas vs the paper's transform. Derived both directions independently for the 1-out-of-t Gaussian: with L ~ N(1/(2s^2), 1/s^2) and D = -L~ ~ N(-1/(2s^2), 1/s^2), remove-loss = ln((e^L + sum_{i<t} e^{D_i})/t) and add-loss = -ln((sum_{i<=t} e^{D_i})/t). alloc_remove (random_allocation.rs:76-103) builds exactly e_d.self_conv(t-1).conv(e_l) then into_pmf_log(t), and alloc_add (105-128) builds from_pmf_exp_neg(l).self_conv(t) then into_pmf_neg_log(t); NormalLoss::gaussian_neg_dual (realization.rs:74-81) is N(-1/(2s^2),1/s^2) as required. Directions verified numerically, not just structurally.

Soundness and tightness of the full-epoch transform. Built a completely independent deterministic reference (geometric-grid convolution with value-preserving mass splitting, scratchpad/exact_ref.py) and compared delta_at: sigma=1.0 -> ratios opaque/ref = 1.0033-1.0045 (t=8), 1.0040-1.0084 (t=16), 1.0053-1.0238 (t=64); sigma=2.0 -> 1.0088-1.0252 (t=8), 1.0057-1.0079 (t=16), 1.0133 (t=64). Never below 1. Cross-checked at t=8 with 5e7-sample Monte Carlo (scratchpad/mc2.py) — agreement within 0.35%, all discrepancies inside 1 standard error.

Soundness and tightness of the prefix (partial final epoch) PLD. Derived the mixture myself: conditioned on the added record's bin B ~ U[t], the released-prefix ratio is (1/t)(sum_{i in R} e^{L_i} + (t-r)) with weight r/t for 'B in R' and (t-r)/t otherwise, which is exactly q_sum/active_sum/weighted_mix_pmfs (random_allocation.rs:214-238). Deterministic reference gives opaque/ref = 1.0035-1.0041 (t=8,r=3), 1.0049-1.0055 (t=16,r=5), 1.0059-1.0075 (t=64,r=7) — a tight, always-valid upper bound. (An earlier Rao-Blackwellised MC suggested a 14% shortfall at t=16,r=5; that was heavy-tail MC noise, refuted by the deterministic reference.)

k>1 block-decomposition bound. Verified the joint-convexity argument: drawing a uniform partition of [t] into k blocks of sizes floor(t/k)/ceil(t/k) and picking one step per block is permutation-invariant, S_t acts transitively on k-subsets, so the induced law on the k-subset is uniform; hockey-stick joint convexity then gives D(P) <= D(P_pi). Confirmed numerically against exact enumeration of all k-subsets with 4e6-sample MC (scratchpad/kmc.py): opaque/true = 1.043-1.805 (t=8,k=2), 1.038-1.302 (t=6,k=3), 1.038-1.237 (t=8,k=4) — always conservative. Block arithmetic m_f*t_floor + m_c*t_ceil == t and m_f+m_c == k verified for all 1<=k<=t<=24 by the crate's own test and re-derived by hand.

Edge cases. t=1 (both alloc_remove and alloc_add short-circuit to the base Gaussian), k=t (block size 1, composes to t-fold Gaussian), k=0 and k>t (rejected by random_allocation.rs:439-447), t=0 (rejected), noise_multiplier<=0/NaN (rejected), max_conv_grid=0 (rejected before the span/0 division at Accuracy::derive:53-57), released_steps=0 or >total_steps (validate_prefix_params:372-393), total_participations outside [1,total_steps] (271-283). Python layer additionally rejects num_bins<2 and n_steps<1 in __post_init__ (so deserialization via cls(**kwargs) is also guarded) and n_steps outside [1, self.n_steps] in pld_at.

negative_infinity_mass propagation (the flagged random_allocation.rs:157-185,250 vs pld/metrics.rs:305,314). Traced it end to end: disc_dist sets negative_infinity_mass=0 (realization.rs:178); GeomPmf::from_pmf_exp maps it to zero_mass=0 and from_pmf_exp_neg maps infinity_mass to zero_mass; under Rounding::Up conv only produces zero_mass from a.zero*b.zero (geom.rs:322), and under Rounding::Down infinity_mass only comes from operands, which are 0. So both the remove and add PMFs leave the transform with negative_infinity_mass == 0, and weighted_mix_pmfs' propagation at line 172 is a no-op in practice. Non-zero left-tail mass only appears after self_compose, bounded by left_tail_budget = tail_mass_truncation/2 = 5e-16 (dense.rs:312,360), which is what pmf_beta_asymmetric silently renormalises away — an effect of order 5e-16 on beta only, not on delta or epsilon.

Directional-rounding soundness of the geometric convolution. Re-derived the index table: with a common ratio R, log(A+iR sum B+jR) = jR + f(i-j), so output bin j+K[d] with K[d] rounded in the requested direction preserves the bound; the d==0 shortcut is safe because the anchor itself is directionally rounded. All sums of two operands lie in [A+B, (A+B)r^(n-1)], i.e. exactly the renormalised grid, so the idx<0 / idx>=n branches are ulp guards rather than routine mass loss. Rounding::Up is used for every remove-direction step and for the outer -ln of the add direction, with Rounding::Down used only for the inner sum that -ln inverts (alloc_add:122-127) — the correct direction in each case.

Truncation floor. beta_total = 0.5*exp(log_mass_truncation_bound) split as beta_total/t across the t convolved copies (Accuracy::derive:58-60), so the epoch PMF's infinity_mass lands at the intended total. Measured infinity_mass = 9.640e-23 (b=64), 9.613e-23 (b=256), 9.625e-23 (b=1024) — i.e. ~0.5*e^-50, independent of t as designed, and 17 orders of magnitude below any realistic delta. Below that floor the transform correctly returns the floor (verified at sigma=2, t=16, eps=2: true 2.4e-29, reported 5.2e-21) rather than an optimistic value.

Runtime sampler vs the PLD assumption, step by step. RandomAllocationSampler._epoch_bins draws `rng.integers(0, num_bins, size=num_samples)` — each record independently uniform over bins, redrawn per epoch via fold_in(key, epoch) — which is exactly 1-out-of-num_bins allocation with independent epochs, matching epoch.self_compose(full_epochs). Bins are emitted in index order 0..num_bins-1 and the partial final epoch emits its first `n_steps % num_bins` slots, matching random_allocation_gaussian_prefix_pld's 'first r released' model exactly. Empty bins are emitted rather than compacted (test_emits_empty_batches) and the trainer still performs a pure-noise optimizer step and still charges the accountant for it (_dp_trainer.py:1766-1802), so releases are never conditioned on non-emptiness.

Prefix/horizon composition arithmetic. `divmod(n_steps, num_bins)` matches the sampler's `divmod(i, num_bins)`; epsilon_at was verified monotone non-decreasing over n_steps = 1..24 at num_bins=16 (scratchpad/probe1.py), continuous across the epoch boundary at 16, and pld_at(num_bins) equals the full-epoch PLD. per_step/Repeated route through repeated_pld -> pld_at(count) rather than composing pld_at(1) count times (composition/_per_step.py:47-76, _repeated.py:60), and repeated_pld rejects count > n_steps.

DDP. The train dataset is sharded with local_shard before the sampler is built (_dp_trainer.py:3658-3668) and the key is folded with the rank, so each record lives on exactly one rank and still lands in exactly one bin per epoch — the 1-out-of-num_bins model survives unchanged, including the documented DDP-resume caveat where every rank restores rank 0's key. Note also that the amplification does not depend on dataset size at all, so dataset trimming cannot desync sampler and accountant here.

ignore_data_skip. `_CURSOR_FREE_SAMPLING_MODES = frozenset({"poisson"})` and TrainingArguments.__post_init__:1055-1064 raises for random_allocation/k_out_of_t, so the fresh-key restart path (which would re-randomise the allocation mid-horizon) is unreachable for allocation samplers.

Serialization round-trip. RandomAllocation serialises through the generic DpProcess codec: an Accountant holding Repeated(PerStep(RandomAllocation(Gaussian(1.1), num_bins=8, n_steps=32)), 20) round-trips through JSON to a bit-identical epsilon (2.98776420 before and after). The sampler snapshot carries key_seed/key_impl/consumed/num_samples/num_bins/n_steps and restores the exact remaining stream; dataset-length mismatch raises. The only gap is the num_bins guard reported above.

Interaction with the inner mechanism. _effective_noise_multiplier resolves NonPrivate and noise_multiplier==0 to a non-private PLD (epsilon=inf, fail-closed), AdaClip(Gaussian) to its exact single-Gaussian effective sigma, and raises TypeError for anything else; the factory validates the inner type as well. (AdaClip's own released-statistic binding is open issue #345 and out of scope here.)

Headline utility claim. 'Amplifies strictly more than poisson at the matched rate 1/num_bins' holds at every point measured: b=16 E=1 alloc 3.050544 vs poisson 3.765670; b=16 E=2 alloc 3.625016 vs 4.458305; b=32 E=1 alloc 2.404655 vs 2.717708 (delta=1e-8, sigma=1.0).

Determinism. The fixed ROW_CHUNKS=64 chunking in geom.rs:225-266 plus ordered fold makes the transform thread-count independent, which the repository test test_random_allocation_reproducible.py exercises across RAYON_NUM_THREADS in {1,2,8}; re-read the code path and confirmed no rayon reduce/work-stealing order dependence remains.

KOutOfTSampler contrast (checked while auditing the shared surface): its sequential r/u selection yields exactly-uniform k-subsets, and unlike RandomAllocationSampler a prefetch cursor offset only *drops* participations, so the k-out-of-t accounting stays conservative under the resume path described in finding 1. Its k>1 prefix conservatism is already tracked by open issues #441 and #693 and is not re-reported here.
